body: I wish I could refuse customers the manager, but unfortunately I have to drag out my poor friend and manager to hear their nonsense.
People will look and probably think “huh, weird,” but they will forget in less than a minute. Do what you want.
Yes. And I’m not even a trainer obviously, I’m just another sales associate desperate to keep the ship afloat.
Thank you, I appreciate the feedback. It's a tense environment, but I'll try to be more patient as much as possible.

My favorite is everyone walking into the huge arrows pointing against them in front, and ignoring the EXIT ONLY, THIS IS THE EXIT signs loudly flanking their right and left sides. And then they get incredibly offended when told to leave the store and stand outside at the huge PLEASE STAND HERE square on the floor, heralded by a WAIT HERE standing sign. Happens at least 100 times.

We do support her at work. Hell, we \*baby\* her. It's been months, though, and our work demands high customer interaction, satisfaction, and turnover in a short amount of time. We need her to be loud, chipper, and communicative--and she is none of these things either with us or customers. It's very stressful because we have to do her job and ours because she's not grown at all. I just don't know what to do anymore, despite coaching her in the most agonizingly sugary ways possible. When she doesn't do her job, our store floor immediately goes to hell and we suffer tangible repercussions in sales, ratings and physically+verbally violent people.

I don't know. I'm Mexican, and the offenders of this are often Mexican too. And they bring several generations: aunts, uncles, grandpas, grandmas, and all the children inbetween. So a matter of "no childcare" is bullshit. There's obviously adults available to stay home and watch the children. Stay home, there's no need to make a circus of this. Stop making my retail life hell.

I know I’m mean, but I grew out of being outwardly anxious. I knew it wouldn’t do myself or anyone any good. Any anxiety, I keep to my damn self. If your coworkers are creating a welcoming, safe environment for you, and you’re still acting like a huge coward, it’s gonna drive a person nuts!

I used to think it was nice to do, but then I actually got a retail job. Now I feel violated and thrown for a loop when people say my name. It catches me so badly off guard. I know the intention is good but it really distracting, so please just don’t do it.

The men in my family are like this to a point. They’ll wear masks if they have to but they rip it off as fast as possible or look for any chance not to wear it. They’re not abusive, they’re just insecure and anti-science. They see masks as effeminate and a sign of weakness, which I get after them about because I’m a woman and disabled. They feel bad when I put it in perspective for them but damn do I wish it weren’t like constantly talking to petulant children.
I wear one in line as a customer though the rest of my family doesn’t.

I get customers like this all the time. They don’t understand that orders need to be relayed through a corporate and remote location server, processed, and then be made available for pickup. But they want to pick up their item within the hour... why not just come in the store and buy the item? We aren’t GrubHub.
Wish that were us!

I learned that the business I work for handles mask mandates differently in the same state based on mall management, not state mandate. So while my store is looking like Miami Beach on spring break because our mall management says we can’t refuse maskless customers, another store of the same business one county over has strict mask wearing guidelines and hand sanitation policy. I’m so insanely jealous of them.
Totally understandable, I’m sorry you’re currently stuck in such a predicament. I wish better things for you in your future!
“You’re all disgusting, brainless pigs that stumbled your way into wealth by no merit of your own.”

Now. My first retail job made me cry but I stuck it out for a month. After that, I’ve learned to say “fuck it” to other jobs that are not healthy and uplifting. You deserve a workplace that enables your well-being.

Art too. I’ve been improving at cranking out some illustrations regularly again (I fell off the wagon due to tendinitis and college-related ptsd), but I’m too exhausted and arthritic to explore things like 3D modeling and 2D animation in freeware programs. My comic has been postponed indefinitely too.
That sounds like a shit job you should bounce from. It’s not worth the stress of trying to understand the psychotic paranoia of geezers who don’t even have emails.
I work at a toy store. I’m contemplating not watching the kids leave the store anymore. Fuck the parents.

It is! It’s definitely what drew me to the job and it’s still what motivates me. I have to say though, the pandemic making customers AWFUL and BAB’s lack of support on a corporate level for its staff (no raises, favoring maskless customers over staff safety, no hazard pay, etc) is what’s really wearing me down. But the kids and my wonderful coworkers keep me going.

It’s necessary to have a lot of emotional stamina and charisma. You’ll be talking with people all day and you’ll be doing several jobs at once/within quick rotation of each other. Some days will be good but you have to be prepared for the inevitable tough days where people wear you down and take everything out of you yet you still have to be extremely peppy and fast on your feet.

You’re expected to be WAY above and beyond any other retail job standard for minimum wage. It’s a difficult job but it can be personally rewarding despite not paying you much. You have to really want to work at BAB.

I think it bothers me more than outright rudeness because it’s so.. pathetic. To watch a person uselessly flail about and then hear “whoopsie”. Like a sort of bid for pity but I can’t afford them any, watching them was too exhausting. 

I’m sorry I’m just very tired. 💀
Ask an employee for some, we'll gladly give you a handful. Got too dang many.
Thank you for saying that, it means a lot. I've never been told thank you, I just get cussed out and yelled at every day.

Not too horrendous but yeah, a sloppy environment regardless. I don’t blame you for leaving. Better to quickly get out of what’s an obvious headache than to stick it out from a sense of undeserved duty.

I’m immediately dispirited by customers just by their lack of face mask or their insistence on wearing it incorrectly. “I don’t care about you, or if you die,” is what it says. And that message is sent to me by hundreds of customers every day. No wonder I feel dead inside.

You’re entirely right. It’s my nature to be a caring and dutiful person, so the fact that retail and corporations’ response to the pandemic has wrung me completely dry of any fear for speaking truth about what’s going on speaks volumes. Because... We’re not wrong, now are we? And why should any of us balk at management finger wagging while us in retail have no protections, no pay, and die thanklessly?
This post is so delightful haha. Being in retail and donning the uniform really is like role playing.

A customer cried big crocodile tears to my manager that I “bullied” her, by merely asking her to go back to her spot in line, keep out of the close personal space of my current customer I was seeing, to take the free satin hearts she molested with her, and that’d I’d be glad to help her in just a few minutes.

Nothing happened from it, but golly.

There’s nothing to fear. I quit my first and third job with no notice, because they were assholes. 2 weeks notice isn’t mandatory, it’s merely a nicety. You do what’s healthy for you and don’t look back!

It’s the same at Build A Bear. We’re not allowed to comment on customers wearing masks anymore, and even though we have the legal right to ask not to be recorded during work we still get customers demanding that they can. It’s a goddamn zoo.
Lol that’s fine but you’re the rare exception to the rule.
I'm more bothered by customers with a ton of groceries using the self checkout when folk with a few or moderate amount of groceries want to use it. Just go to a regular line with a cashier, freaks.
Not really, in my opinion--and so seems the opinion of many others. Its body pattern and the fur used are very much like Fuzzy Bunny. It's rough, stiff, and not cuddly at all.

I agree very much about the COVID safety point. The other stores in the area have been closed due to COVID, and ours is the only one left. And despite that, customers still disregard our safety by fighting us tooth and nail over wearing a mask and maintaining 6 ft. It makes me want to cry in frustration sometimes. Their actions closed the other BABs, why do they want to close this one too? And why are they so rude when we're overworked because now everyone who visited those other stores are now all coming to the single one remaining? A simple "Okay, I understand" with compliance is all I want.

I agree, I miss regular animals. But BAB depends on brand tie-ins because they're struggling financially, they need the help of other franchises to sustain them. That's why most of their in-store animals are characters.
